explanation: The theorem says that `toBilin' (Matrix.J l ℤ)`, the standard symplectic form on ℤ^(l⊕l), is a perfect pairing. Mathlib has the general tools: `LinearMap.IsPerfPair.of_bijective`, `IsPerfPair.compl₁₂`/`congr`, `Basis.toDualEquiv`, and `J_squared` in `Matrix.SymplecticGroup`. But I found no lemma at the matrix level, for example "the bilinear form of an invertible matrix (one with unit determinant) is a perfect pairing". I looked for one by grepping `IsPerfPair` together with `toBilin'`, `toLinearMap₂'`, `det` and `Matrix.J` across Mathlib. Only six files mention `IsPerfPair`, and none of them gives a matrix criterion. In `LinearAlgebra/Matrix/{BilinearForm,SesquilinearForm}` the lemmas about `Matrix.Nondegenerate.toBilin'` and `toLinearMap₂'` only give nondegeneracy, which over ℤ is weaker than being a perfect pairing. The library's proof has to put the result together from several of these ingredients, so it is not a one-line instance of a single Mathlib declaration.
